name: Banh ngao
summary: Bánh ngào is a hot molasses rice cake for cool or drizzly weather, sweet, chewy, and gingery. One account gives it no filling; another allows mung bean, pork, or none.
origin: Nghệ An, and an afternoon snack on the Vinh city portal’s 24 November 2022 page.
taste: The city portal says molasses, chewy sticky rice, and ginger. Vietnamnet says sweet, chewy, rice, and ginger. VnExpress says the molasses is red, boiled with ginger, and very sweet.
howToEat: Eat it hot, in cool weather or a drizzle. The eight-specialty article says you blow on a small bowl. Vietnamnet, 27 November 2023, says the cake is glutinous rice and molasses, a cocoon or an oval, with no filling, chewy, sweet, and gingery, coated in molasses rather than stuffed. VnExpress, 4 September 2016, says rice flour rolled round like bánh trôi, dropped into boiling molasses and ginger so it soaks, which is why it is called ngào, and that mung-bean, pork, and empty cakes are all served. That article printed about 10,000 đồng at markets.
where: The 24 November 2022 city page puts it in the afternoon and does not name a street. VnExpress says the markets and does not name which hall. Check on arrival.
seoTitle: Banh ngao in Vinh — molasses rice cake
seoDescription: Bánh ngào is a hot molasses rice cake for cool or drizzly weather, sweet, chewy, and gingery.
